I literally have no idea what a 'Nen ability' is, or have seen Hunter x hunter. It's unwise to assume people are copying things from niche pop culture if it's similar.

Secondly, this was written six years ago, back when site standards we're incredibly different.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is very similar to the Ortho Siblings' Nen ability from Hunter x Hunter. Damage corresponds to spots on the board, it can be actively targeted, the dart rules need to be obeyed and failure leads to the damage being returned to the user.

Though, that being said this is different enough that I don't mind much since the MC&D angle is neat. At the same time this isn't really outstanding in terms of writing or execution either, so I'm gonna novote.

EDIT: I realize I worded this clumsily - I'm not assuming that there's inspiration here, I'm just pointing out that there is a lot of similarity there because it's an interesting coincidence that such an out-there idea appeared in two different places like this. I should've said "…that being said even if this is inspired by the HxH thing…" or something like that.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Figured out exactly what it did as soon as I read the title, and the article itself only continued to disappoint. Much like SCP-772, I'm only left questioning why this had to be tested on humans rather than any number of animals first. Animals can be named. Unless there's some indication that it only works on humans, then even then I fail to see what warrants dozens of tests. It's a board you throw the dart on the board, person goes "owwee" and breaks their body. I cannot imagine any remotely useful information to be gleaned by repeating the test 80 times over
